title: Thai Red Prawn Curry
subtitle: Fast weeknight Thai curry
excerpt: A quick, vibrant Thai red curry of king prawns, coconut milk, and green beans that is ready in under 30 minutes. The key technique of frying the paste in coconut cream before adding the liquid gives the sauce its deep, rounded flavour.
sourceNotes: Red curry is one of the most popular Thai curry styles, characterised by a paste of dried red chillies, lemongrass, galangal, and shrimp paste. The coconut milk base and fresh herbs distinguish it from Indian-style curries. Prawn versions are among the quickest to prepare as the seafood cooks in minutes.

content.text: Open the coconut milk tin without shaking it. Spoon the thick cream from the top into the wok first; this is what you fry the curry paste in. The cream is richer in fat and will allow the paste to fry properly rather than just stewing in liquid. Add the prawns right at the end; they turn rubbery if overcooked.
Spoon the thick coconut cream from the top of the tin into the wok. Heat over a medium-high heat until the cream sizzles and starts to separate.
Add the red curry paste and kaffir lime leaves. Fry, stirring constantly, for 2 to 3 minutes until the paste is deeply fragrant and the oil separates from the paste.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and 100ml water. Bring to a simmer.
Add the red pepper, green beans, fish sauce, and palm sugar. Simmer for 5 minutes until the vegetables are just tender.
Add the king prawns and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until they are pink and curled. Do not overcook.
Squeeze in the lime juice and scatter over the thai basil. Serve immediately with jasmine rice.

items.cause: They were overcooked in the hot sauce.
items.fix: Add prawns last; remove from heat as soon as they turn pink.

items.cause: Coconut milk was added before the paste was properly fried.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes; the sauce will thicken slightly.

items.symptom: Curry paste tastes raw and harsh.
items.cause: It was not fried for long enough in the coconut cream.
items.fix: Fry paste for a full 3 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
